headline: Computational tools resolve isoforms, splicing and polyadenylation from RNA-seq data
label: Isoform Resolved Transcriptome Tooling
summary: Recent preprints and database papers add computational methods for splicing, polyadenylation and intronic transcript structure from RNA-seq data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving transcript-level structure from RNA-seq and carrying it into downstream interpretation. splicelogic converts differences between transcript sets into discrete events such as exon skipping and intron retention. MOCHI applies a reference-independent k-mer framework to strand-specific short-read data to curate candidate independent intronic transcripts. scPolyA and IsoAPA address alternative polyadenylation, the former in single-cell and spatial 3' transcriptomes and the latter as a long-read atlas of 2.3M transcript-resolved polyadenylation sites across 816 sample groups. scSpAS integrates ATS, splicing, APA and full-length isoform regulation in single-cell and spatial contexts. R2T2P links genome-guided transcriptome assembly to translation profiling and proteomics. The newer element is the shift from isolated event calling toward integrated, multi-layer resources. The AlphaGenome promoter perturbation study serves as a cautionary counterpoint, showing that CAGE and RNA-seq predictions decouple with weak propagation to downstream exons.
